dedupe_keys.name: surficial bed sediments and water in the navigation pools of the upper mississippi river 1991 1992 usgs open file report 95 708

description: USGS Open-File Report 95-708, edited by John A. Moody and published in 1997, compiles hydrologic, sedimentologic and chemical data on the surficial bed sediments and water of the navigation pools of the Upper Mississippi River. Coverage: composite samples from the downstream third of the 25 sampled navigation pools between Minneapolis, Minnesota, and St. Louis, Missouri, collected from July 1991 to April 1992, plus samples from the Lower Mississippi and some tributaries. Contents: sampling strategy for shallow and deep water, discharge, mixing and flushing rates of the pools, particle size and bulk chemistry of the bed sediments, organic carbon, and later chapters on sterols, polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons and other contaminants. Format and access: a 288-page PDF with data tables, free from the USGS Publications Warehouse (DOI 10.3133/ofr95708). Licence and cost: US government work, free. Caveats: a one-off survey from the early 1990s, tables are in PDF, not machine-readable files, and bed conditions changed after the 1993 flood. The particle sizes and pool characteristics can describe channel bed material for sediment, dredging and scour inputs in hazard exposure and network flow models of the lock and dam navigation system. It relates to the USACE Lock Performance Monitoring System in the catalogue.
